subject: Banking
title: The $81 Million Bangladesh Heist
description: A fast breakdown of The $81 Million Bangladesh Heist for builders.

hook.text: In 2016, hackers stole $81 million from Bangladesh's central bank by sending fake SWIFT messages to the New York Fed.

buildup.text: The attackers gained access to Bangladesh Bank's SWIFT terminal and sent 35 fraudulent transfer requests totaling $951.

discovery.text: A spelling error in one request raised a flag. The word 'fandation' instead of 'foundation' stopped most transfers.

twist.text: Five transfers totaling $81 million went through before anyone noticed.

climax.text: A typo saved $870 million. The heist exposed that even the world's most secure payment network has human weak points.

punchline.text: A typo stopped $870M in theft. $81M still vanished through SWIFT.

quiz.question: What accidentally prevented the full $951 million theft?
options: A spelling error in a transfer request raised suspicion
